newsitem.title: FRANCE: ONIC sees 3.25 pct grain area increase this year.
newsitem.headline: ONIC sees 3.25 pct grain area increase this year.

text.p: French cereals office ONIC on Wednesday trimmed its forecast for the 1997 increase in grain area from the previous estimate but said sowings would still be more than three percent higher than last year.
In a monthly report, ONIC projected a total 1997 grain area of 8.992 million hectares, up 3.25 percent from 1996. Last month it had projected a rise of 3.38 percent.
The change was based mainly on an upward revision in last year's area to 8.708 million hectares from 8.698 million, rather than any significant change in this year's overall forecast.
Among the main cereals, ONIC projected a 4.13 percent rise in winter and spring soft wheat area to 4.950 million hectares -- barely changed from last month's 4.1 percent growth forecast.
It peggged winter and spring durum sowings at 256,840 hectares, down 4.79 percent from 1996 compared with a 3.71 percent fall projected last month.
Winter barley was raised a notch to 1.612 million hectares, up 5.57 percent on 1996, compared with a previous annual growth estimate of 5.08 percent.
Maize sowings settled up 0.87 percent at 1.731 million hectares, a modest increase from last month's data showing a 0.8 percent sowing increase.
